### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest`, touching **69** documentable anchor(s).

**36** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 61b12584f043032ee750ba140c9ce71405955283`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **10** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **43** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 61b12584f043032ee750ba140c9ce71405955283` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ac88b62d60ece9b34fa90395688e6171803479fa` — the merge of head `b85b0914dbdeb18ede19f46ff4d54d1a438f3f3e` into base `61b12584f043032ee750ba140c9ce71405955283`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ac88b62d60ece9b34fa90395688e6171803479fa && git checkout ac88b62d60ece9b34fa90395688e6171803479fa
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 61b12584f043032ee750ba140c9ce71405955283 b85b0914dbdeb18ede19f46ff4d54d1a438f3f3e && git checkout -B drift-repro 61b12584f043032ee750ba140c9ce71405955283 && git merge --no-ff b85b0914dbdeb18ede19f46ff4d54d1a438f3f3e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 61b12584f043032ee750ba140c9ce71405955283
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 61b12584f043032ee750ba140c9ce71405955283` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b85b0914dbdeb18ede19f46ff4d54d1a438f3f3e`
Local-runs: none

The head has not moved since the brief. Read: the net diff `origin/main...head` (17 files, +1547/−436), the PR body, the card inputs the brief names, the #23398 body and triage 6163659502, and ADR-0131 D10–D12 on `origin/main`. Check-runs on the head as of 2026-10-14T09:50Z: 25 success, 6 skipped, **1 failure**, **7 in progress**.
- **FAILED:** "The card this PR closes must claim this branch": "PR #23452 closes #23398 with no `Claim:` on the card naming `claude/issue-15211-c7b-promotions`".
- **RUNNING:** Test Core (1/6) through (6/6), and Type Check · workspace.
- The PR is a draft; GitHub reports it mergeable.

### ① Derived judgments

**F1 · blocking: S1 makes the ceremony refuse on every 17.x database.**
- **The change.** `environment-overlay-duplicates` now groups by `bundle_member`. `planCategory` calls `requireColumn` on every groupBy column, against the PHYSICAL columns (`pragma_table_info` / `information_schema`), and refuses with `missing-column`.
- **Why nothing adds the column first.** Both the plan and the apply boot with `deferSchemaDdl`, so no schema sync runs before the plan.
- **Who lacks it.** `sys_metadata.bundle_member` arrived in 5677add93f (#22954). It was first released in 18.0.0-next.0, and no 17.x tag contains it.
- **The effect.** The plan refuses `sys_metadata`, and so does `--apply`, which plans first. That happens on exactly the databases the ceremony exists to migrate.
- **How the PR hid it.** It added `ALTER TABLE sys_metadata ADD COLUMN bundle_member TEXT` to two existing fixtures that modelled that shape: the plan integration seed, and the apply test "holds a column whose rows another stage owns". `readMetadataKeyRows` already treats the column as optional; the category does not.
- **Against #23398.** #23398's rehearsal on v17 copies (pin 5b68524b93) reached `column-drops` on `main`. With S1 it would stop at the plan (inferred from the tags, not run).
- **Remedy.** Group by `bundle_member` only when the column is present, and restore a fixture without it as the pin.

**F2 · blocking: version lineages are not unique environment-wide after the run (Q2 A).** `runVersionRenumber` shifts only items that already hold two or more lineages when it runs (`group.length` under 2 is skipped). The door numbers an environment save from environment-scoped history (`nextItemVersion`, `organization_id IS NULL`). So any later environment save on an item whose only lineage is an organization's starts at version 1, inside that organization's 1..n. Four paths reach it:
- **(a) The carry onto a code-served view** whose key differs from the organization row's. Under a wall that is every carry, because nothing is skipped. Under `single` it happens across packages, which is the dogfood's own shape: a package-less organization row beside a packaged code view.
- **(b) A two-organization conflict with no environment lineage, chosen and carried.** The organizations are laid out 1..n and n+1..m, and the environment save takes 1.
- **(c) The template promotion,** where an organization's `email_template` lineage exists and no environment one does.
- **(d) Runtime saves, until S2 drops the column.** Every runtime save of a promoted lone item lands the same way. That item's rollback also cannot see its own snapshots, which stay organization-tagged.

Why the pin and the dogfood missed it:
- The ⭐ carry pin plants an environment lineage (`h_env1`, `h_env2`). Remove those two rows and the pin's own `duplicates()` reads non-empty.
- The dogfood planted an environment lineage too.

The PR body says "none of the ceremony's own environment saves … can land on a number an organization holds", and the changeset claims uniqueness. Both are false for versions.

**F3 · blocking: a conflict resolved to an organization row beside an environment row is neither fail-closed nor crash-safe (Q1 B).** `resolveMetadataConflict` promotes the chosen row first. When the chosen row is an organization's and an unchosen row is the environment's (the usual `single` conflict), two environment rows hold one key until the delete. The overlay index is NULL-distinct on `organization_id`; triage 6163659502 calls this Catch 1.
- **(a) The carry can land on the wrong row.** The view carry then saves through the door. The door picks its write head with `findOne` on (type, name, `organization_id` NULL, state, package), which the repository's own #8907 note calls a driver-order coin toss.
  - If the save lands on the unchosen row, the withdrawal is written there and deleted with that row. The chosen row keeps the form open.
  - The fail-closed pin covers only the other direction (the environment row chosen), and its fake door always wins.
- **(b) A crash between the promotion and the delete is not recoverable by a rerun.**
  - On the rerun no organization row is left in the group, so `groupMetadataKeyRows` drops the conflict.
  - `validateMetadataChoices` then refuses the same `--metadata-choice` ("names no row awaiting a choice").
  - Without that flag, the step reports done over a duplicate environment pair.
  - `column-drops` then blocks on `environment-overlay-duplicates`, with no ceremony remedy. The only way out is hand SQL on a table whose API allows get and list only.
  - The rerun is not idempotent, and none of this is pinned.

**The promotion (Q6 A, posture).**
- **Under `single`:** lone organization keys are promoted in place by an UPDATE conditioned on the owner. Pinned.
- **Under a wall:** a lone row is promoted only when it is named. The rest are reported in `notes` and hold the column. Pinned. `walled` is `posture !== 'single'`, so an unknown posture fails safe.
- **The one path that does not read the posture:** a chosen conflict. Under a wall, choosing one organization's row deletes the other organizations' rows of that key. Q1 B is unqualified, but Q6 A's text says "unchosen rows stay reported and blocking; the ceremony never deletes them". The PR does not name this and does not pin it under a wall: see ③.
- **Should-fix: the conflict key ignores `state`.** Active uniqueness is `WHERE state = 'active'`. Yet a draft or archived row beside an active row of the same key is listed as a conflict, and the operator's choice deletes it, though nothing collides.

**Conflicts (Q1 B).**
- **The normal path holds:** the choice resolves the conflict, and the unchosen rows are deleted by id only after the promotion is read back. A pin holds the write order.
- **A crash between the two:** F3 (b).
- **Rows the plan did not list:** a deletion targets the candidates computed at APPLY time, not the plan file's list. A row that joins the key between the plan and the apply (an environment save) is deleted on a choice it was never reviewed under. This is a landing-order item with S4.
- **Unnamed and stricter than the stage plan:** an organization row and an environment row with identical bodies are a conflict too. The stage plan said "with a different body".

**The form-withdrawal carry.** It runs under every posture, before the promotion, through the door, judged by `anonymousFormIntakeWithdrawnIn`. A door refusal blocks (pinned), and a rerun carries nothing twice (pinned). It is not fail-closed in three places:
- F3 (a).
- **Under `single`, a key held by both a withdrawing organization row and an open environment row is skipped** (`heldByOrganization`). It waits for the operator's choice. Meanwhile the doors no longer read the organization layer, so the form is open from the upgrade until that choice. The skip's stated reason ("a door save there would make a conflict of a promotion") holds only for a key the organization holds alone.
- **Unparsable organization bodies** (`parseBody` returns null) are silently not carried. This is minor.

**The history renumbering (Q2 A).**
- **`event_seq` is sound.** It is unique after a full run. `sequence-renumber` runs after the last ceremony save and again on every apply (the between-runs pin). It is idempotent on a rerun and after a kill between the commit and history writes (pinned).
  - Minor and unpinned: a kill mid-step, followed by an environment save before the rerun, changes the offset. Commits already moved are not moved again, so their ranges end up off by the difference.
- **Versions:** see F2.
  - Each `version-renumber` run is idempotent, but the step is checkpointed and never re-run, so it cannot catch a lineage created after it.
  - The dogfood's exact self-collision (numbers just given to an organization) is closed and pinned. The same class, through a lone organization lineage, is open.

**The deleted organization read on the form doors.** No caller outside the tests is left, on `main` or at the head.
- `legacyFormOrganizationId`, `LegacyFormViewsRequest` and `anonymousFormOrganization` survive only in tests that pass the key on purpose (with casts), and in released CHANGELOG and pre-changeset text.
- The price of the deletion: a database not yet migrated serves organization-only withdrawals open. The changeset says so, but nothing forces the ceremony until S5's boot refusal (#23413 Q3 A) ships.

**#23398.**
- **The Ask, under `single`:** met. The `organization-presentational-promotion` category is consumed before `column-drops`.
- **Under a wall:** met only row by row, with `--metadata-choice`. The category's label still reads "promoted to environment rows", with no wall.
- **The title's "column-drops blocks on sys_metadata forever"** stays true until S2 (#23429), for another reason (the declared column). The PR says so.
- **Verdict:** F1 stops the plan on the 17.x databases #23398 was measured on. `Fixes #23398` is not honest at this head.

**Tests.**
- **Ablations:** each of the eight reddened its named pin. Four of them ran on an earlier head; the dev says those code paths are unchanged.
- **Holes:**
  - No pin guards the read-back before the delete. The order pin checks write order only, so removing the read-back reddens nothing.
  - F1 through F3 are unpinned, and F1's pin shape was edited away.
  - The ⭐ pin for ruling #22008 A judges a re-implemented door predicate over a fake list. The real doors were exercised once, by hand.
- **Existing `--apply` runners on `main`:**
  - `apply-flags`: unaffected; it asserts no step list.
  - `fate-supplement`: mocks the apply.
  - `utils/schema-migrate.one-shot-family.integration.test.ts`: runs a real `--apply`. It sits outside the dev's `organization-ownership*` and `commands/migrate` runs. Its verdict is in Test Core, still running.

**Cross-stage: landing-order items (S4 is #23437, not landed).** None is a FAIL for S1 by itself.
1. **The digest catches a stale plan.** S4's digest covers the inventory (stage plan 6162468695). S1 changes the inventory, so S4 refuses a plan file made before S1. That refusal is loud and correct.
2. **The digest does not cover what the apply deletes.** `--metadata-choice` and the conflict lists computed at apply time are outside it, so a reviewed plan does not bind which rows the apply deletes. Whichever lands second should refuse a choice whose conflict's candidates differ from the plan file's `metadataConflicts`. `--template-choice` has the same gap, which is S4's own.
3. **If S4 lands first,** S1's changeset example needs `--plan-file plan.json`.
4. **Both edit the same files:** `organization-ownership.ts` and `organization-ownership-apply.ts`, and its test. Whichever lands second merges `main`.
5. **S2 must drop its renumbering copy** (5326201df). The duplicates F2 leaves would make S2's `(type, name, version)` unique index fail at boot. The reopened-withdrawal window lasts until S5.

### ② Semver level

The changeset grades `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/rest` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` all `patch`, with `Clause-②: no`. Against WHICH LEVEL in `pr-automation.yml`, on the v18 `next` line, that is wrong in both directions:
- **A widening.** The plan payload of `os migrate organization-ownership` shipped in cli 18.0.0-next.0 (cc305a3). S1 adds two things to it:
  - `metadataConflicts`, a new key on `TablePlan`, pinned in the plan integration test;
  - `--metadata-choice`, a new accepted flag.

  A new key on a published payload takes at least `minor`. The precedent is PR 3's changeset for the same shape (`--template-choice` and `templateConflicts`, with `--apply` equally unreleased), which is `minor` with `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. The PR's argument ("`steps[].step` values do not widen a released contract") holds for the apply report only.
- **A narrowing.**
  - `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.getMetaItems`, which the package index exports, loses `legacyFormOrganizationId` from its parameter type. That type shipped in 18.0.0-next.0 (c8b062f011), and the PR's own tests now need casts to pass the key.
  - The anonymous doors close more: on a deployment with no organization, one package's withdrawal now closes every package's form.
  - Before the ceremony runs, the doors serve organization-only withdrawals open.
  - The changeset describes these behaviours, but carries no `(narrowing)` arm, no BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 marker.
- **What it should carry:** `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `@objectstack/cli: minor`, a BREAKING banner with the FROM → TO line for the removed key, and one ADR-0087 disposition marker.
  - The alternative is a written seat ruling that the protocol-internal key is not a published surface. Even then, `yes (widening)` and cli `minor` stand.
  - The changeset also does not mention F1's new plan refusal.

### ③ Boundary flags

**From report 6165486835** (no open questions):
- **Out of scope 1:** the `--seed-admin` grants block `rewrite` on a seeded showcase database (6163356782). Whether it is carded is NOT MEASURED. Escalated to the seat, because it blocks every `--apply` dogfood on a seeded showcase.
- **Out of scope 2:** S2's renumbering copy is superseded. Answered as landing-order item 5.
- **Acceptance notes:**
  - "`--plan-file` omitted": answered as landing-order item 3.
  - "Not a released contract": wrong for the plan payload (see ②).
  - "Not S1's": agreed. Those items are S2's.

**Unnamed deviations** (the seat ratifies or rejects each):
- `version-renumber` lays out two organizations' lineages even with no environment lineage, beyond Q2 A's "only where an environment lineage … exists". This is needed for uniqueness.
- Identical-body pairs are conflicts.
- The carry skip under `single` covers conflicted keys too.
- The `bundle_member` re-key is named in the body, but its F1 consequence is not.

**Escalations:**
- **Q6 A against Q1 B under a wall.** A walled conflict's choice deletes another organization's row.
- **Two conflict lists in one plan.** `organization-presentational-conflicts` still groups (type, name) across organizations only, while `metadataConflicts` groups the overlay key and includes the environment. Pointer 6020279837 says there is one conflict list.
- **The withdrawal window until S5.** Ruling #22008 A says the read goes "in the same change", but S5 lands later. The seat either accepts the window in writing or holds S1's release until S5.
- **ADR-0131 D10 still calls mirror deletion "the one deletion this record sanctions".** Q1 B adds a second. The ADR text is #23403's.

**Before the queue:**
- a `Claim:` on #23398 naming the branch, for the failed check;
- Test Core and Type Check · workspace to finish.

**NOT MEASURED:**
- the running checks, including the one-shot family `--apply` test;
- the physical shape of real 17.x databases (inferred from the tags);
- the repository's write-head choice in F3 (a) (read, not run);
- `legacyFormOrganizationId` callers in objectstack-ai/cloud and objectui;
- the posture of #23398's rehearsal databases;
- the dev's first four ablations on the final head.

**Seat adoption** (2026-10-14T10:02Z). Adopted after an audit of the reviewer transcript: one Write, to this record only; 63 Bash calls, all reads (`git show`, `git diff`, REST GETs); no MCP call, no GitHub write, no worktree, build or test run. The seat re-read F1 in the diff: `conflictBy.groupBy` names `bundle_member` unconditionally, and two fixtures gain `ALTER TABLE sys_metadata ADD COLUMN bundle_member`. The seat rules:
- **F1, F2, F3:** fix in this PR, each with a pin that starts from the state the finding names: a 17.x table without `bundle_member`; an item with only an organization history, then an environment save; a crash between the promotion and the delete, then the same `--metadata-choice` again.
- **The wall (Q1 B against Q6 A).** The ruling of record 6163114098 says, for `isolated` and `group`: "unchosen rows stay reported and blocking; the ceremony never deletes them". That clause is specific to a wall, so it governs there. Under a wall a chosen row is promoted and nothing is deleted. Q1 B's delete applies under `single`. Pin both. This applies the ruling's own text. It is not a new answer, and the director can overturn it.
- **The reopened forms window.** This is a question of ordering between technical tasks, so the seat decides it without escalation. S1 keeps the form doors' organization read. Its deletion moves to S2 (#23429), the stage that drops the column and lands with S5's boot refusal, so no release serves an organization-only withdrawal open. A pointer goes to #23429.
- **② follows from that.** With the read kept, `getMetaItems` keeps its parameter, and the narrowing leaves S1. The new `metadataConflicts` plan key is a widening: `minor`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, the PR 3 precedent.
- **S4, which lands first.** S1 lands second, so it carries the merge with S4. After it, an apply's deletions must come from the reviewed plan: `--metadata-choice` is covered by S4's plan file and digest, the way `--template-choice` is or is made to be. The changeset example carries `--plan-file`.
- **`Fixes #23398`** stays. The seat posts the claim that the closing-card check asks for when S1 is ready to land.
